subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by adding per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` semantics, by folding the need into per-agent/A2A allowlist work, or by keeping the current single visibility scope?
rationale: The source limitation is real, but the fix changes a security-sensitive public config boundary and overlaps active per-agent and allowlist session-authorization proposals.

options.title: Choose one granular session-permission model
options.body: Approve a single schema that covers send/history/list/status semantics and require schema, docs, and tests to land together.

options.title: Defer to per-agent/A2A scoping
options.body: Treat open per-agent and A2A allowlist work as the product direction, then close or narrow this issue after that direction is accepted.

options.title: Keep the single visibility scope
options.body: Reject granular session permissions for now and document that cross-agent send requires the same visibility level as list/history/status.

recommendation.title: Choose one granular session-permission model
recommendation.body: Approve a single schema that covers send/history/list/status semantics and require schema, docs, and tests to land together.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent and feature-history evidence most consistently connects this person to the session-visibility and config surfaces that need the product/security decision.
